subtype: Approach: values-first planning about saving versus spending [Thinking]
passage:
Amandeep: I keep saying flat, flat, flat. You keep saying trip. That's the fourth time we've had this fight.
Bhupen: Because a life without trips isn't one I want to save for.
Amandeep: And to me the flat is the reason we work.
Bhupen: What if we stop arguing about who's right and ask what each thing is for? For me a trip is feeling free.
Amandeep: And the flat is feeling safe.
Bhupen: Then what if sixty percent of what we set aside goes to the flat, and forty to travel?
Amandeep: Sixty and forty. Can we look at it again in a year?
Bhupen: Deal. One good trip a year is still real.
Amandeep: And I don't feel I've lost the flat.

qa.q: What split did Amandeep and Bhupen agree on?
qa.a: They agreed on sixty percent to the flat and forty to travel.

qa.q: What does the flat mean to Amandeep, and how does Amandeep feel about it?
qa.a: The flat means feeling safe to Amandeep, and Amandeep is relieved that it has not been given up.

qa.q: What else could the couple do to keep the agreement working, and why?
qa.a: They could review it after a year as agreed and note what each goal has given them, because priorities may shift.

qa.q: How might Bhupen have felt when the trip was kept in the plan?
qa.a: Bhupen was probably relieved and appreciated, since travel stayed a real part of the plan and not a dismissed wish.

grounding: Illustrates a couple with different money priorities agreeing a percentage for each goal after asking what saving and travel mean to each, so neither feels dismissed.
